newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's SBI driven higher by Lek jump.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's SBI driven higher by Lek jump.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index rose on Thursday, pulled up by an almost three percent jump in market heavyweight drug maker Lek.

"The same buyers (foreigners), as last week resumed their activity, which was expected after they withdrew for a few days in order to push prices lower. I expect shares to oscillate over the next week," said Robert Rudolf, a trader at brokers Moja delnica.
The SBI blue-chip rose 1.85 percent or 26.05 points to 1,431.02.
"The index could reach as high as 1,700 points by September, but not more than that, and I expect autumn to be stormy," Rudolf said.
Traders said foreign investors, widely regarded as long-term buyers, would continue buying even if parliament fails to ratify the EU association agreement before July 15.
"Slovenia will definitely join the union sooner or later so it (ratification) does not make a big difference for those who are buying on a long-term basis," one broker said.
Parliament is expected to vote on changes to the constitution on Monday in order to allow foreigners to own land, and ratification of the association agreement is expected to follow swiftly.
Overall 10 shares rose, nine fell and one was flat while eight were untraded. Turnover rose to 430.4 million tolars from 314.4 million.
Lek had the highest turnover, rising 2.84 percent to 32,930 tolars on volume of 7,262 shares for total turnover of 239.4 million tolars.
Traders said Lek was likely to move between 31,000 and 33,000 tolars.

Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were top gainers jumping 3.08 percent to 13,400 tolars on volume of 30 shares, while bank's ordinary shares eased 0.80 percent to 14,800 tolars on volume of 70 shares.

"Dolenjska banka's shares might be one of hidden stars on the market as they are generally seen as one of the most underpriced regarding the bank's performance and outlook especially after Daiwa was allowed to buy in," one broker said.
Financial consultancy Primofin led decliners, tumbling 7.89 percent to 7,000 tolars on volume of only five shares.
